title: Depleted Korea knock out Japan before China retain Asian men's team title
standfirst: Without three of their leading men, Korea beat world No. 1 Sora Matsushima's Japan in the semi-finals, then lost 3-0 to China in the final. Japan won the women's event.
body: China retained the men's team title at the Asian Championships in Tashkent, beating Korea 3-0 in the final. The scoreline hides a strong week for the Koreans, who reached the final without Shin Yu-bin, Lim Jong-hoon or Jang Woo-jin and knocked out Japan on the way.

Korea beat India 3-0 in the quarter-finals, then upset a Japanese side including world No. 1 Sora Matsushima 3-1 in the semi-finals. Kang Dong-soo won both of his singles, against Hiroto Shinozuka and Tomokazu Harimoto, and Park Gyu-hyun beat Matsushima 3-0.

China were too strong in the final. Zhou Qihao beat Kang 3-1, Lin Shidong beat Park Gyu-hyun in straight games, and Xiang Peng closed out the tie with a 3-1 win over Park Kang-hyun. Two of the games went to extra points, but Korea did not win a match.

Star News Korea reported that the silver was Korea's sixth in the men's team event at the Asian Championships and the first since Yogyakarta in 2019. Kang plays his club table tennis for Samsung Life and Park Gyu-hyun for Mirae Asset Securities.

In the women's event, Korea took bronze after losing 3-0 to China in the semi-finals, having beaten India by the same score in the quarter-finals. Japan won the title, beating China in the final, according to Butterfly's report.

The team events opened a tournament that ran from 19 to 25 October and also served as Asian qualification for the 2027 World Championships. Japan later recovered in the individual events, with Harimoto winning the men's singles and Matsushima and Miwa Harimoto taking the mixed doubles.

sources.name: Butterfly: China wins 4, Japan wins 3 at Asian Championships
